name: Congenital Pancreatic Cyst

criteria.description: Identification of a unilocular or multilocular cyst within the pancreas on imaging studies
Histological confirmation of cyst lined by true pancreatic epithelium without evidence of neoplasia
Exclusion of infectious, neoplastic, or pseudocyst causes by clinical and laboratory evaluation
Presence of abdominal mass or symptoms related to cyst compression

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic pancreatic cyst on imaging plus histopathological confirmation of epithelial lining and exclusion of other cyst types
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires surgical biopsy or resection for definitive confirmation.

laboratory: Normal or mildly elevated serum amylase and lipase
Absence of infection markers unless cyst infected
imaging: Ultrasound showing well-defined cystic lesion in pancreas
MRI/CT demonstrating unilocular or multilocular cyst with thin walls
No solid components or septations suggestive of neoplasm
genetic: May be associated with developmental anomalies
other: Histopathology showing cyst lined by cuboidal or columnar pancreatic epithelium
Absence of inflammation or neoplastic cells in cyst wall

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of true epithelial lining on histology
Presence of solid components or mural nodules on imaging
Cystic dilatation of bile ducts rather than pancreas

redFlags: Signs of cyst infection or abscess formation
Onset of obstructive jaundice or pancreatitis
references: Kumar V, Abbas AK, Aster JC. Robbins Basic Pathology. 10th Edition. Elsevier; 2018.
Pediatric Pancreatic Cysts: Diagnosis and Management. Journal of Pediatric Surgery. 2020;55(6):1102-1108.
